p: A trip to the coast with toddlers and preschoolers is all about rhythm. Too much sun or wind and they wilt; too long in one spot and they get bored. Having a covered play area to slot into the middle of the day is a real lifesaver, giving them a change of scene and you a chance to regroup, top up drinks and dig out the spare clothes.

The trick is to mix the outdoor and indoor bits. Beach and paddling in the morning while the little ones are fresh, lunch, then a stint in soft play when the sea breeze picks up or energy starts to dip. By the time you've had a final ice cream on the prom, there's a decent chance of a peaceful journey home.

Sand gets everywhere at the seaside, and soft play centres won't thank you for bringing half the beach in with you, so give feet a good brush off and pop socks on before heading inside. Keep a small bag of essentials handy: wipes, drinks, a snack and a change of clothes for anyone who manages to get soaked at the water's edge.

Clacton is well set up for families, with long sandy beaches that slope gently into the sea and plenty of space to spread out away from the busiest patches near the pier. The clifftop gardens and the prom make for easy pushchair walking. A short drive along the coast takes you to the quieter beaches of Holland-on-Sea and Frinton-on-Sea, and Walton-on-the-Naze, which has its own pier, a sandy beach and the striking Naze Tower on the clifftop.
